sections.title: Occam bounds and the distinction from minimum description length

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-occam-learning-C012 (partial): The method does not state all of its hypotheses, so the failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The steps in def:p15-occam-method (handbook/parts/p15/occam-learning.tex lines 251-255) never require that the m training observations be independent draws with the population law P. That is the hypothesis of def:p15-occam-model at lines 20-21, and item 1 of thm:p15-occam-boundaries (lines 213-216) shows the guarantee fails without it. Even so, the conclusion at lines 257-258 claims 'the stated probability over the sample'. The steps also never require fixing a target-size bound n with l(f) <= n, which puts the target in the fixed represented class. The 'required output-size' bound n^c m^a (line 130) depends on n, and so do the sample sizes of thm:p15-occam-compression (lines 147-151) and thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation (lines 171-173). As written, 'choose the sample size from the applicable theorem' cannot be carried out from the listed steps. The method lists the learner-side premises and the fixed-before-sampling premise as explicit steps but leaves out these data-side premises. The sibling methods do state the sampling assumption: def:p15-conc-reference-method (bounded-concentration-learning.tex 444-445) and def:p15-w02b-p15-064-method (statistical-learning-and-generalization-w02b-p15-064.tex 362-363).
